message.content:
The original square has area \(49\), so its side length is

\[
\sqrt{49}=7.
\]

Folding one pair of opposite corners together makes the crease be the other diagonal of the square. When unfolded, the square is divided into two congruent right triangles, each having:

- two legs equal to the square’s side length: \(7\) and \(7\),
- hypotenuse equal to the square’s diagonal: \(7\sqrt{2}\).

So the perimeter of one triangle is

\[
7+7+7\sqrt{2}=14+7\sqrt{2}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{14+7\sqrt{2}}\).
